lab_and_purpose.purpose: for the determination of xanomeline concentrations in plasma
lab_and_purpose.method: each sample will be centrifuged at approximately 177 × G for 15 minutes. The plasma will be transferred into a polypropylene tube ... capped and frozen at approximately −20°C

evidence.quote: Blood samples (7 mL) for the determination of xanomeline concentrations in plasma will be collected from each patient at Visits 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, and 11.
The blood sample drawn at Visit 3 is a baseline sample.
Immediately after collection, each sample will be centrifuged at approximately 177 × G for 15 minutes.
The plasma will be transferred into a polypropylene tube bearing the identical label as the blood collection tube.
Samples will be capped and frozen at approximately −20°C.
The samples will be shipped on dry ice to Central Laboratory.
Plasma concentrations of xanomeline will be determined from samples obtained at selected visits (Section 3.9.2).

instruments.name: Alzheimer’s Disease Assessment Scale - Cognitive Subscale
instruments.version: ADAS-Cog (14) (the 11-item ADAS-Cog (11) plus delayed word recall, attention/visual search task, and maze solution); subset ADAS-Cog (11)
instruments.respondent_or_rater: administered by a health care professional trained to do so; involves interviewing the patient alone
instruments.scoring_or_range: The maximum total score is 90. 70 points are possible on the cognitive section and 20 points on the attention/concentration section. The higher the score, the greater is the degree of cognitive impairment. ADAS-Cog(11) is a 0-70 scale.
instruments.purpose: an established measure of cognitive function in Alzheimer’s Disease; ADAS-Cog (11) is a primary efficacy instrument, ADAS-Cog (14) a secondary efficacy instrument

evidence.quote: Alzheimer’s Disease Assessment Scale - Cognitive Subscale (ADAS-Cog): ADAS-Cog is an established measure of cognitive function in Alzheimer’s Disease.

For the purposes of this study, three items (delayed word recall, attention/visual search task, and maze solution) have been added to the ADAS-Cog (11) to assess the patient’s attention and concentration.
The 14 item instrument will be referred to as the ADAS-Cog (14).
The ADAS-Cog with attention/concentration tasks should be administered by a health care professional trained to do so.
The test will take approximately 30-45 minutes to complete and involves interviewing the patient alone.

The maximum total score is 90. 70 points are possible on the cognitive section and 20 points on the attention/concentration section. The higher the score, the greater is the degree of cognitive impairment.
For example, ADAS-Cog(11) is a 0-70 scale.
The ADAS-Cog (11) and the video-referenced CIBIC+ will serve as the primary efficacy instruments. Secondary efficacy instruments will include the DAD, the NPI-X, and the ADAS-Cog (14).
P = Practice only - It is recommended that a sampling of the CIBIC+, ADAS-Cog, DAD, and NPI-X be administered at Visit 1.

instruments.name: Video-referenced Clinician’s Interview-Based Impression of Change
instruments.respondent_or_rater: clinician (at least one year of experience with the instrument, blinded to all other efficacy and safety measures); semi-structured interviews with the patient and caregiver
instruments.scoring_or_range: global numeric score on a 1 to 7 scale (1 = marked improvement; 4 = no change; and 7 = marked worsening)
instruments.purpose: an assessment of the global clinical status relative to baseline; primary efficacy instrument

evidence.quote: The CIBIC+ is an assessment of the global clinical status relative to baseline.
The CIBIC+ used in this study is derived from the Clinical Global Impression of Change
The instrument employs semi-structured interviews with the patient and caregiver, to assess mental/cognitive state, behavior, and function.
aggregated in the assignment of a global numeric score on a 1 to 7 scale (1 = marked improvement; 4 = no change; and 7 = marked worsening).
The clinician assessing CIBIC+ will have at least one year of experience with the instrument and will remain blinded to all other efficacy and safety measures.
A semi-structured interview should be used to assess global change.
Circle the number that indicates the extent of change, if any, observed since the initial baseline interview.
P = Practice only - It is recommended that a sampling of the CIBIC+, ADAS-Cog, DAD, and NPI-X be administered at Visit 1.

instruments.name: Revised Neuropsychiatric Inventory
instruments.version: revised from its original version (Cummings et al. 1994)
instruments.respondent_or_rater: administered to the designated caregiver by a health care professional trained to do so
instruments.recall_period: the worst condition of the patient in the time period since the most recent NPI-X administration
instruments.mode: at clinic visits or via a telephone interview
instruments.scoring_or_range: Frequency 1-4 (Occasionally to Very Frequently); Severity 1-3 (Mild to Marked); Distress 0-5 (Not at all to Very severely or extremely); total score computed by taking the product of the frequency and severity scores and summing them up across the domains (primary total excludes the sleep, appetite, and euphoria domains)
instruments.purpose: an assessment of change in psychopathology in patients with dementia; secondary efficacy instrument

evidence.quote: The NPI-X is an assessment of change in psychopathology in patients with dementia. The NPI-X is administered to the designated caregiver.
This instrument has been revised from its original version (Cummings et al. 1994)
NPI-X will be administered at 2-week intervals either at clinic visits or via a telephone interview.
Xb = Performed at this visit and via telephone interview 2 weeks following this visit.
The NPI should be administered by a health care professional trained to do so.
The NPI is administered at every clinic visit, plus twice via the telephone when patients are not required to come to the clinic.
The answers pertain to changes in patient’s behavior that have appeared since the onset of the illness.
represent not the condition of the patient at that moment in time, but rather the worst condition of the patient in the time period since the most recent NPI-X administration.

The primary assessment of this instrument will be for the total score, not including the sleep, appetite, and euphoria domains. This total score is computed by taking the product of the frequency and severity scores and summing them up across the domains.
4. Very Frequently - once or more per day.
3. Marked - delusions are very disruptive
5. Very severely or extremely

instruments.name: Disability Assessment for Dementia
instruments.recall_period: over a period of 2 weeks up to the time of the interview
instruments.scoring_or_range: Yes = 1, No = 0, Non applicable (N/A) = 96; total score and component scores reported as percentage of items that are scored “1”; subscores of initiation, planning and organization, and effective performance
instruments.purpose: to assess functional abilities of activities of daily living (ADL) in individuals with cognitive impairment; secondary efficacy instrument (a third primary variable in Europe)

evidence.quote: The DAD is used to assess functional abilities of activities of daily living (ADL) in individuals with cognitive impairment.
The DAD is administered to the designated caregiver.
The DAD is administered through interview with the caregiver in a quiet environment.
The DAD is a measure of the actual performance in ADLs of the individual as observed over a period of 2 weeks up to the time of the interview.
Yes = 1 No = 0 Non applicable (N/A) = 96
DAD is a 40 item questionnaire where each question is scored as either “0” or “1”. The DAD total score and component scores are reported as percentage of items that are scored “1”.

The DAD will be analyzed with respect to the total score, as well as the subscores of initiation, planning and organization, and effective performance. This variable is considered a secondary variable in the US, but is a third primary variable in Europe.
P = Practice only - It is recommended that a sampling of the CIBIC+, ADAS-Cog, DAD, and NPI-X be administered at Visit 1.

The scoring range for the MMSE is 0-30.

instruments.name: Hachinski Ischemic Scale
instruments.respondent_or_rater: completed by the physician based on clinical information obtained from diagnostic information and physical examination
instruments.scoring_or_range: Scores for the 13 items are added together for a total score. Patients who score 5 or greater are more likely to have a dementia of vascular etiology and are excluded
instruments.purpose: to better distinguish multi-infarct dementia (MID) from other types of dementia; screening tool

evidence.quote: The Hachinski Ischemic Score (Hachinski et al. 1975) was devised to better distinguish multi-infarct dementia (MID) from other types of dementia
The Ischemic Score is based on a 13-item scale

The Hachinski Ischemic Score is to be completed at Visit 1 (screening visit). The scale should be completed by the physician based on clinical information obtained from diagnostic information and physical examination.
Scores for the 13 items are added together for a total score. Patients who score 5 or greater are more likely to have a dementia of vascular etiology and are excluded from participating in the trial.
[4] Hachinski Ischemic Scale score of ≤4 (Attachment LZZT.8).

measurements.name: Vital signs
measurements.position_or_condition: Patient should lie supine quietly for at least 5 minutes prior to vital signs measurement; Patient should then stand up; standing blood pressure and heart rate after approximately 1 and 3 minutes
measurements.method: Blood pressure measured in the dominant arm with a standardized mercury manometer according to the American Heart Association standard recommendations (an automated blood pressure cuff may be used if regularly standardized); diastolic blood pressure as the point of disappearance of the Korotkoff sounds (phase V); heart rate measured by auscultation

evidence.quote: vital signs (including supine/standing pulse and blood pressure readings)
Vital signs, temperature, and an assessment of adverse events will
Patient should lie supine quietly for at least 5 minutes prior to vital signs measurement.
Blood pressure should be measured in the dominant arm with a standardized mercury manometer according to the American Heart Association standard recommendations.
Diastolic blood pressure will be measured as the point of disappearance of the Korotkoff

sounds (phase V). Heart rate will be measured by auscultation. Patient should then stand up. Blood pressure should again be measured in the dominant arm and heart rate should be measured after approximately 1 and 3 minutes.
An automated blood pressure cuff may be used in place of a mercury manometer if it is regularly (at least monthly) standardized against a mercury manometer.

measurements.name: 12-lead ECG
measurements.method: 12-lead ECG; interpreted at the site and express mailed overnight to a central facility

evidence.quote: All patients will be screened by obtaining a 12-lead ECG, and will have repeat ECGs performed at Visits 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, and early termination (ET)
ECG data will be interpreted at the site and express mailed overnight to a central facility which will produce a report within 48 hours.

measurements.name: 24-hour Ambulatory ECG
components: AV block (first, second, or third degree)
measurements.position_or_condition: at Visit 2 (prior to the initiation of study medication); minimal recording period for an interpretable ambulatory ECG 8 hours, of which at least 3 hours must be sleep
measurements.method: 24-hour Ambulatory ECG; data express mailed overnight to a central facility

evidence.quote: All patients will undergo a 24-hour Ambulatory ECG at Visit 2 (prior to the initiation of study medication).
The minimal recording period for an ambulatory ECG to be considered interpretable will be 8 hours, of which at least 3 hours must be sleep.
At Visit 3 the Ambulatory ECG will be removed
Several outcome measures will be extracted and analyzed from the Ambulatory ECG tapes, including number of pauses, QT interval, and AV block (first, second, or third degree).
The number of pauses greater than or equal to 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 seconds will be tabulated.

notes: Single protocol version: Protocol H2Q-MC-LZZT(c) (title page and every running header); the SoA (Attachment LZZT.1, pages 53-54) is part of it. No separate amendment or other protocol version is in the PDF; exclusion criteria numbered with a 'b' suffix ([16b], [27b]-[31b]) appear to be revised criteria but no amendment text says what changed. nct_id: the input is identified only as CDISC_Pilot; the protocol prints no NCT number, so 'CDISC_Pilot' is recorded and the schema's NCT pattern is not met (not invented). cross_references: empty — the SoA input has no cross-references (soa_cross_references is empty). abbreviations: the protocol has no abbreviation list. Entries are those defined under the SoA tables (pages 53, 54), in the lab-tests table Table LZZT.1 (page 32, incl. CS/NCS in the note below it), and IDDM (page 14, needed for the lab table's 'IDDM patients only'). SoA-name tokens not defined by these entries but expanded in the body text: MMSE (Mini-Mental State Examination, p11), TTS (Transdermal Therapeutic System, p1/p5), ADAS-Cog (p27), CIBIC+ (p28), NPI-X (p7/p28), DAD (p7/p28). Never expanded anywhere: 'Apo E', 'Chem/Hemat' (read as chemistry/hematology from p9 wording) and 'A1C'. Lab-tests table (Table LZZT.1, page 32) runs two columns together in the text layer; page 32 was read from the page image (rule 10) and analytes assigned to panels from it — the image confirms the text-layer order (left column Hematology then Urinalysis; right column Clinical Chemistry, Thyroid Function Test, Other Tests). No page lacks a text layer. Specimen for hematology and urinalysis is not stated; chemistry is printed as 'Serum Concentrations of'. Central laboratory is stated only for folate, Vitamin B12 and thyroid function tests (exclusion [28b], p15) and for the xanomeline plasma samples (p29). Conflict (rule 5), Hemoglobin A1C: SoA note Xa and p8 say insulin-dependent diabetics; Table LZZT.1 says 'IDDM patients only'; exclusion [30b] (p16) says required on patients with known diabetes mellitus or random blood sugar >200 on screening labs. All recorded with evidence. Conflict, NPI-X schedule/recall: p27/p8 2-week intervals at clinic or by telephone and SoA note Xb (telephone 2 weeks after the visit); p75 says administered at every clinic visit plus twice via telephone. Recall: p43 'worst condition ... since the most recent NPI-X administration' vs p75 'changes ... since the onset of the illness'. DAD scoring: p81 gives N/A = 96 while the worksheet header (p82) prints Not Applicable=N/A. SoA rows the text does not describe beyond being performed: Habits (no mention anywhere in the text), Chest x-ray, Medical History, Physical examination (no components stated), Patient number assigned (p24 identification number), Study drug record, Medications dispensed/returned, Concomitant Medications, Adverse events, Laboratory (Urinalysis) (visits only), Placebo TTS test (p24 describes acute tolerance test, not a lab/instrument/measurement). Not linked to an SoA activity and therefore not recorded as instruments: the skin rash questionnaire (p31, p33-34) and NINCDS/ADRDA guidelines (Attachment LZZT.7, diagnostic criteria). Syphilis screening method (RPR then confirmatory FTA-Abs, p16) is recorded on the Other Tests panel. Updated 2026-11-07 to schema 1.1 (no re-extraction): instruments carry kind; nct_id null (no NCT number printed).
